fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Minutes showed almost all officials expect more hikes, and Goolsbee left a larger-than-usual rise open after hot October inflation. Then the AI-led stock rout erased half-point bets and Bessent warned the Fed risks overtightening, so the committee weighs raising rates into a correction, with this week's PCE reading still to land.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US presidency convenes it after Trump's Shenzhen summit with Xi and Putin, billed as a nuclear summit, brought three of its leaders to one table, and after COP31 deadlocked over a fossil-fuel transition and finance for developing economies. What this summit settles is whether either thread reaches the wider group.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: France's borrowing premium over Germany has hit 1.75 points and the bank has so far left Paris to the markets; this meeting shows whether that stance holds. It comes days after Paris and Berlin settled the succession, with Spain taking the presidency and Germany's Markus Brunnermeier the chief economist seat.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: UK inflation accelerated again in the latest reading and has now topped target for more than two years. The committee meets with that overshoot lengthening rather than fading, and the decision settles how much longer the Bank of England will tolerate it before the cost of credit for UK households and firms has to answer for it.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: The yen breached 160 per dollar this month, and Washington sold $500 million of euros to buy it. A weak yen is now inflating the cost of Japan's defence plan and its flagship AI project, while core inflation came in at 2.2%, under the 2.3% forecast. The Bank of Japan weighs a currency squeezing the state's budget against prices that came in softer than expected.

fred-us-gdp-2026-11-25.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's measure of US output, published each quarter as an advance estimate and then revised twice. It sets the growth figure the Federal Reserve, Treasury yields and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-gdp-2026-11-25.recent: Reports going into the holiday season say US consumers are holding up against inflation, and household spending is the largest piece of this figure. The release settles how much of that resilience reached output, the growth reading the Fed weighs alongside prices.

fred-us-pce-2026-11-25.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on US personal income and spending, which carries the PCE price index the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. It sets the inflation read that rate expectations and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-pce-2026-11-25.recent: US consumers went into the holiday season still spending in the face of inflation. This release puts figures on that: how much households earned, how much they spent, and how fast the prices they paid rose. It settles whether incomes are keeping pace with that spending.

fred-us-gdp-2026-12-02.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's measure of US output, published each quarter as an advance estimate and then revised twice. It sets the growth figure the Federal Reserve, Treasury yields and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-gdp-2026-12-02.recent: US consumers have been reported holding up against inflation going into the holiday season, and household spending is the largest part of what this release measures. It settles how much of that resilience showed up as actual growth, the reading the Fed weighs alongside inflation.

fred-us-jobs-report-2026-12-04.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly Employment Situation report, usually out on the first Friday, counts nonfarm payrolls and sets the unemployment rate. Treasury yields, the dollar and Fed rate bets move on it within seconds.
fred-us-jobs-report-2026-12-04.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the month's payroll count and unemployment rate. The release settles whether hiring kept its pace or slowed, and it is the last full read on the labour market before the year closes.
